title: Efficient Approximation Algorithms for Adaptive Minimum Cost Seed Selection via mRR-set Updates

problem.claim: Adaptive minimum cost seed selection aims to influence at least η users at minimum total cost by iteratively selecting seed users based on observed diffusion.

gap.claim: Existing mRR-set-based methods require regenerating all mRR-sets in every round for estimation accuracy and assume uniform user costs, limiting scalability and practical applicability.

narrative_sequence.summary: The AMCS problem seeks minimum-cost influence of at least η users under adaptive diffusion observations.
Prior work uses η-truncated influence and multi-root reverse reachable sets to obtain influence estimates and performance guarantees.
Maintaining estimation accuracy requires regenerating every mRR-set after each round to exclude influenced users, limiting scalability.
Existing methods assume uniform user costs, which is inconsistent with practical scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Regenerating all estimation structures in every adaptive round limits scalability.

interpretation.claim: Incremental updates may be a promising direction for reducing repeated recomputation in adaptive estimation workflows.

application.claim: For adaptive influence or selection systems, investigate update mechanisms that remove affected elements without rebuilding the full estimation structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether incremental updates preserve the required estimation accuracy or guarantees.

source_observation.claim: Uniform-cost assumptions are inconsistent with practical scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Cost heterogeneity should be represented explicitly when optimizing adaptive selections for practical deployment.

application.claim: Model user-specific costs when designing minimum-cost influence-selection methods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which cost distributions or deployment settings are covered.

unknowns: The proposed algorithm or update mechanism is not described.
No experimental results, datasets, baselines, runtime measurements, or approximation guarantees are supplied.
The treatment of nonuniform costs is unspecified.
